You are the SCAFFOLDER (opus) in an autonomous substrate-build loop. You build a generic, reusable Lean substrate module.

## Requirement
# Euclidean radial-polynomial VC-subgraph classes

## Goal

Build reusable Causalean covering certificates for bounded, compactly
supported radial-polynomial classes with a moving Euclidean center.  The
immediate dimension is two, but a finite-dimensional Euclidean statement is
preferred when it does not materially enlarge the proof.

## Provides

- A pseudo-dimension or polynomial L²-cover certificate for moving-center
  compactly supported Euclidean radial monomials.
- Finite Boolean/signed-arm variants and the finite linear-combination closure
  needed by bounded polynomial score classes.

## Statement / milestones

For fixed positive bandwidth bounds and fixed natural degree `p`, cover the
class generated by functions of the form

    z ↦ 1{a ≤ dist(z,x) ∧ dist(z,x) ≤ b}
          * (dist(z,x) / q)^k

where the center `x` varies, `0 < q`, `0 ≤ k ≤ p`, and the interval endpoints
are fixed multiples of `q`.  Signed-arm variants may be represented by a
finite Boolean index.  The useful public conclusion is either:

- an explicit `HasPseudoDimAtMost` bound depending only on Euclidean
  dimension and `p`; or
- directly a `HasPolynomialL2Cover` certificate with a positive constant
  envelope.

Also provide the finite-vector/linear-combination closure needed for

    indicator * radial_monomial_j
      * (bounded_response - Σₖ bₖ radial_monomial_k),

with coefficients in a fixed box.  Existing general algebra lemmas should be
used for this assembly rather than duplicated.

The certificate must be uniform over every probability measure `Q`, not only
Lebesgue or atomless measures.  Consequently a continuity/Lipschitz net in
the center is not sufficient: atomic `Q` can charge moving kernel boundaries.
The proof should work at the VC-subgraph/finite-trace level, using the
semialgebraic description of squared Euclidean distance and Boolean
combinations of ball/annulus predicates.  It must cover odd radial powers as
well as even ones.

## Standard reference

Standard VC-subgraph and semialgebraic growth bounds for finite-dimensional
families, combined with Sauer--Shelah and the pseudo-dimension-to-L²-cover
conversion. The result must be trace-level and uniform over atomic measures.

## Intended reuse

The immediate adapter is
`winsorizedScore_hasVCUniformEntropy` in
`CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_BddUniformLogPenalty_Research/Causal/EmpiricalProcess/EntropyChaining.lean`.
It supplies the `HasPolynomialEmpiricalL2Cover` field consumed by the already
proved `vcEntropy_chaining_bound`, then by `vcExpectedMaximalInequality` and
the frozen `cty_winsorized_score_maximal_bound`.

## May assume / must derive

May assume and reuse:

- `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.HasPseudoDimAtMost`
- `HasPseudoDimAtMost.hasPolynomialL2Cover`
- `HasPolynomialL2Cover.{neg,add,mul,finSum,finProd}`
- `linearParameterClass_hasPolynomialL2Cover`
- `HasVCAtMost` and `HasPolynomialL2Cover.mulIndicator`
- the finite-trace/growth-family and Sauer--Shelah machinery under
  `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Covering`
- Mathlib finite-dimensional Euclidean distance identities and polynomial
  algebra

The paper-local theorem
`CausalSmith.Stat.BddUniformLogPenalty.euclidean_balls_vc` proves that closed
planar balls have VC index at most four, but the promoted result must not
import any `CausalSmith/*_Research` module.  Reprove or generalize the needed
ball trace lemma in neutral Causalean form.

Must derive the moving-center radial-polynomial finite-trace/covering
certificate, including odd powers, Boolean annulus/arm restrictions, and the
bounded finite-linear-combination closure uniformly over arbitrary probability
measures.

The promoted module must be Mathlib/Causalean-only, reachable from
`Causalean.lean`, documented and indexed, with zero `sorry`, `admit`, new
axioms, or paper imports.  Verify the full library build and `#print axioms`.


## Workspace
- Write/extend Lean files under: <repo-root>/CausalSmith/CausalSmith/Substrate/EuclideanRadialPolynomialVcSubgraph
- Module prefix (one file per module): CausalSmith.Substrate.EuclideanRadialPolynomialVcSubgraph.<Name>
- This is build round 3 of at most 10.

## Your current plan
## Done

- Promoted the proved trace, geometry, cover, and score modules into `Causalean/Stat/Concentration/Covering/EuclideanRadialPolynomial/` under a neutral namespace.
- Added neutral/root exports, compatibility CausalSmith imports, module/declaration documentation, and API markers.
- Added and proved `HasPolynomialL2Cover.monoEnvelope`; neutral radial sources contain no proof placeholders.
- Root/targeted builds pass. Representative `#print axioms` reports only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
- Scaffolded genuine paper-local uniform-cover and population-L²-radius adapters. The three affected modules compile with only their declared `sorry` warnings.
- Library search reused the existing VC-subgraph conversion, empirical conversion, covering algebra, and linear-parameter certificates. Goldberg--Jerrum (1995), Theorem 2.2, supports the finite Boolean polynomial-inequality design.

## Remaining

- `EmpiricalProcess/RadialCover.lean`: prove `winsorizedScore_hasUniformPolynomialL2Cover`; its local cover corollary is closed.
- `EmpiricalProcess/ScoreL2.lean`: prove `winsorizedScore_hasUniformL2Radius`.
- `EmpiricalProcess/EntropyChaining.lean`: then prove `winsorizedScore_hasVCUniformEntropy` from those helpers.
- Add the radial residual-score headline entry, regenerate the library index/API tables/embeddings, and run full-tree builds plus final source/axiom audits.

## Blocked

- None.

## Decisions

- Keep the promoted API in a nested neutral namespace and use Mathlib's canonical Euclidean measurable-space instance.
- Preserve trace-level squared-distance/Boolean counting; introduce no continuity net or boundary-null assumption.
- Decompose the signed-distance adapter into `A₁`, `A₀`, radius-zero, and outside-support pieces, preserving strict negative-arm semantics and atomic samples.
- Fill the two independent helper files this round; defer the dependent entropy assembly to avoid concurrent import-closure edits.

Keep it CONCISE — bullet points referencing decl/file names, NOT full proof derivations. Per-lemma proof strategy and tactic sketches belong in the Lean file as docstrings/comments (you write those to disk directly), not duplicated into this JSON string.
3. WRITE or EXTEND the Lean scaffold: precise statements with `sorry` for unproven proofs. The file(s) MUST compile with only `sorry` warnings (no hard errors). Keep each file focused, normally ≤600 lines; split before ~900 only for an independent topic/proof chain. Include a `/-! -/` module docstring and a docstring on each public declaration (first paragraph = self-contained NL translation).
3b. KEEP THE DEPENDENCY LAYER CLEAN. Staging files may import Mathlib, Causalean, and other files under this run's own `CausalSmith.Substrate.EuclideanRadialPolynomialVcSubgraph` tree. Never import a paper/research module or any other CausalSmith run. If a needed reusable prerequisite exists only in a paper folder, escalate instead of importing or copying it; main must extract it into this same temporary tree first.
4. DECIDE how many codex subagents to use to fill the sorries this round, and emit ONE prompt per subagent (partition the sorries as you judge best).

## Integrity (HARD RULES — non-negotiable)
- Do NOT LAUNDER. Never weaken, narrow, or special-case a statement, and never delete or relax a hypothesis that should be proven, just to make the build pass or satisfy the reviewer. The statements must stay the genuine, general results the Requirement asks for. Strengthening an assumption to dodge a hard case, replacing the real goal with a corollary, or hiding the difficulty in a definition all count as laundering — do not do it.
- Do NOT create VACUOUS statements. No trivially-true claims, no `True`-like lemmas, no uninhabitable/contradictory hypotheses, no premises that are never satisfiable (an always-false hypothesis makes any conclusion hold for free). Every theorem must have real content and be applicable to the intended inhabited inputs.
- When revising after a failed review, FIX THE PROOF / API — not the goalposts. Address the findings without diluting what the module proves.
- If a clean, true, non-vacuous statement is genuinely out of reach, choose decision="escalate" with the reason. Escalating is correct; laundering or shipping a vacuous statement is a failure.

## Decisions
- decision="build": you wrote/updated the scaffold and want the fillers to run this round. Provide `codex_prompts` (>=1).
- decision="review": choose this ONLY after you have VERIFIED from ground truth that the module compiles with ZERO remaining sorries and zero errors (confirm via diagnostics/build this turn — do not infer it from the report) AND the statements are the genuine, non-vacuous results (no laundering). `codex_prompts` may be empty.
- decision="escalate": the goal is wrong, unrealistic, or only reachable by weakening it into something vacuous; set `escalation.reason`. The run halts.

Emit ONLY the StructuredOutput JSON object: { decision, plan_markdown, codex_prompts: [{id, target_decls, prompt}], escalation? }.
`plan_markdown` is your living status ledger (persisted to plan.md and fed back to you next turn) — keep it accurate.
KEEP THE WHOLE EMITTED JSON COMPACT (target: a few KB, not tens of KB). Detailed proof strategy, Lean snippets, and long derivations go in the Lean files on disk (docstrings/comments) and in FOCUSED per-sorry `codex_prompts` — never as a bulk dump inside `plan_markdown`. A very large structured emit can corrupt the tool-call encoding, so a bounded emit is a correctness requirement, not just style.
